skip_list.comment: fails on $262.createRealm()

Async test failures newly detected after fixing the test262 runner to check async results regardless of exit code (github.com/facebook/hermes/issues/1982). The last test fails because the lowered generator state machine routes generator .return() through the exception handler, which closes destructuring iterators with ignoreInnerException=true. The spec requires that return completions NOT ignore inner exceptions from IteratorClose (step 7), but the lowered form cannot distinguish return from throw completions. The five eval-var-scope-syntax-err tests fail because Hermes does not support direct eval with lexical scope (emits compile-time warning `Direct call to eval(), but lexical scope is not supported`); the `var` declaration inside direct eval never hoists into the enclosing function scope, so the parameter-binding conflict that should trigger SyntaxError is invisible. Sync counterparts have the same limitation.

skip_list.comment: These are rest failing tests in mjsunit that we may support soon.
Tests rely on outdated spec where String.prototype methods looked up well-known Symbol methods on non-Object arguments. The current spec only performs the lookup when the argument is an Object.

Promise subclassing (PromiseCapability via this) is not supported. Static methods (all, allSettled, any, race, reject, resolve) and prototype.then always use the built-in Promise constructor instead of reading 'this'. This breaks constructor dispatch, capability validation, resolve/reject element functions, iterator close on resolve throw, and same-thenable resolution ordering.

skip_list.comment: Iterator helper incompliance.

Array.prototype.sort is broken for exotic arrays with accessors/proxies. The internal swap uses deleteComputed which fails on non-configurable properties, throwing TypeError instead of handling them per spec.

Missing ArraySpeciesCreate constructor type-check. Methods like concat, filter, map, slice, splice, flat, flatMap do not validate that the resolved constructor is an object before calling it, so non-object/poisoned constructors don't throw TypeError as required.

Array edge cases: length coercion ordering (defineProperty on length doesn't match spec error/coercion order), toLocaleString strict-mode this-boxing (primitives not boxed correctly), unshift near integer limit, and Array.prototype.with iteration edge cases.
TypedArray change-array-by-copy methods (toReversed, toSorted, with) are not implemented. All fail with 'undefined is not a function'.

TypedArray detached buffer handling is incomplete. Operations on TypedArrays whose ArrayBuffer is detached during callbacks (filter, forEach, map, reduce, includes, indexOf, etc.) throw TypeError instead of handling the detached state per spec. Constructor detach-during-coercion tests crash (SIGABRT) or throw wrong error types. Internal methods don't check for detachment before operating.

TypedArray exotic object internal methods ([[Get]], [[Set]], [[HasProperty]], [[DefineOwnProperty]], [[Delete]], [[GetOwnProperty]]) do not properly validate numeric index keys per spec. For invalid indices (out-of-bounds, non-integer, -0, canonical invalid index), they fall through to OrdinaryGet/OrdinarySet instead of returning undefined/false. Reflect.set with wrong receiver type incorrectly succeeds.

TypedArray @@species constructor is not supported. Methods like map, filter, slice, subarray that should create results via the species constructor always use the original constructor, so subclass return type tests fail.

TypedArray constructor edge cases: buffer-ctor-access validation for cross-type construction, custom prototype fallback when proto is not an object, negative length handling, object-arg iterator coercion ordering, and prototype-constructor identity.

TypedArray.from iterator error handling is incomplete. Errors during iteration (access, invoke, next, value) are not properly caught. Cross-realm from, from with mapping/string/iterable sources also fail.

Staging SpiderMonkey TypedArray tests: cross-realm method access, sort edge cases (NaN, modifications, detach during sort), seal/freeze/integrity, toLocaleString formatting, set-with-receiver, slice conversion, has-property, getter-name, write-out-of-bounds, toString, and other behavioral differences.
